# Game over again - clicking (33,15) with player at col 15 failed
# Pattern: clicking blocks too close to player causes game over
# But the board resets to initial state after game over

# New hypothesis: maybe I shouldn't click green blocks at all
# Maybe the goal involves moving the player and clicking purple targets

# Reset first
result = action(['ACTION7'])
seg = current_frame.segmentation
player = [n for n in seg['nodes'] if n['color'] == 'b']
purple = [n for n in seg['nodes'] if n['color'] == 'p' and n['pixels'] == 12]
green = [n for n in seg['nodes'] if n['color'] == 'N']

print(f"Reset: Green={len(green)}, Purple={len(purple)}")
if player:
    pc = sum(pt[1] for pt in player[0]['boundary']) // len(player[0]['boundary'])
    print(f"Player col: {pc}")

print("\nMoving to col 15...")
result = action(['LEFT'])
player = [n for n in current_frame.segmentation['nodes'] if n['color'] == 'b']
if player:
    pc = sum(pt[1] for pt in player[0]['boundary']) // len(player[0]['boundary'])
    print(f"Player col: {pc}")

# Now try clicking the purple target at (8, 15)
print("\nClicking purple target at (8, 15)...")
result = action([{'action': 'MOUSE', 'row': 8, 'col': 15}])
print(f"Result: go={result.get('game_over')}, lc={result.get('level_completed')}, done={result.get('done')}")

seg = current_frame.segmentation
purple = [n for n in seg['nodes'] if n['color'] == 'p' and n['pixels'] == 12]
green = [n for n in seg['nodes'] if n['color'] == 'N']
print(f"After: Green={len(green)}, Purple={len(purple)}")

# Check if anything changed
if not result.get('board_changed'):
    print("Board did not change - clicking purple targets doesn't work")
</parameter>
</function>
